move.evidence:
What is proven, and where

Every controller drives the SAME global path -- one file, its hash checked in every run -- on the same robot with the same speed, turn-rate and acceleration limits.

Evidence: coco_lab_ros/test/test_lab5.py::test_each_scenario_names_a_frozen_path_that_matches_it; coco_lab_ros/test/test_lab5.py::test_no_controller_gets_a_faster_or_more_agile_robot

Every number in the comparison is recomputed from the recording at site build by coco_lab; a bundle whose numbers do not reproduce is refused.

Evidence: coco_lab/test/test_movebundle.py::test_a_metric_that_does_not_reproduce_is_refused; coco_lab/test/test_movemetrics.py::test_box_clearance_axis_aligned_and_rotated

The moving person is seen by the LiDAR but has no collision geometry: it cannot push the robot. A contact is measured, from ground truth, as a clearance of zero.

Evidence: coco_lab_ros/test/test_lab5.py::test_the_actor_has_no_collision_geometry; coco_lab/test/test_movemetrics.py::test_an_actor_walking_through_the_robot_is_a_contact; docs/RESULTS.md "COCO Lab Phase 6"

After every change and every move, D* Lite's plan costs exactly what Dijkstra finds from scratch on the new map.

Evidence: coco_lab/test/test_dstarlite.py::test_dstar_lite_is_optimal_after_every_change_and_move; coco_lab/test/test_replan.py::test_every_round_agrees_with_astar_from_scratch

A robot whose map only lacks obstacles (never invents them) reaches the goal whenever the world has a route, and never steps into a cell it could have known was blocked.

Evidence: coco_lab/test/test_replan.py::test_an_optimistic_robot_arrives_iff_the_world_has_a_route

Same answer, not always less work. Over 200 seeded Sketch worlds D* Lite's total work was below A* from scratch in 191 (median 0.59 of A*'s), yet in 188 of 2204 single replans it did more; and on the real costmap change of Experiment C it touched 3,209 cells where A* from scratch touched 1,114.

Evidence: docs/data/lab5/replan_sketch_stats.json; docs/data/lab5/replan_c.json; docs/RESULTS.md "COCO Lab Phase 6"; coco_lab/test/test_replan.py::test_every_round_agrees_with_astar_from_scratch

The controllers

DWB (Dynamic Window). Samples (v, w) pairs it can reach within one control step (819 per cycle with the mission's settings), rolls each forward 1.5 s, scores each with critics -- obstacle cost, distance to the path and the goal, alignment, oscillation -- and drives the best. A critic can reject a candidate outright.

gazebo_models/config/nav2_params.yaml (controller_server.FollowPath, the mission's, unchanged); coco_lab_ros/test/test_lab5.py::test_the_overlay_adds_two_controllers_and_changes_nothing_else

MPPI (Model Predictive Path Integral). Samples 2,000 noisy control sequences 2.8 s long, scores each whole trajectory with critics, and AVERAGES them, weighted by exp(-cost / temperature). The command is a blend of good trajectories, not the single best one.

coco_lab_ros/config/nav2_move_overlay.yaml (MPPI)

Regulated Pure Pursuit. Chases a point

run15.history:
History: run 15, as it was recorded

From COCO's 20-run fetch matrix (M6, in the v1 wedge world). The robot had picked its target and was driving home when AMCL put it 3.4 m from where it really was — in a corridor the map deliberately left featureless. The global planner still had a path. The local controller rejected every single candidate:

DWBLocalPlanner: No valid trajectories out of 819!
PathDistCritic: None of the 5 first of 5 (5) points of the global plan
GoalDistCritic: None of the points of the global plan were in the local costmap.
	run 15 (failed)	run 11 (same colour, succeeded)
ground truth, map	(8.747, 0.149)	(−0.085, 0.016)
AMCL believed	(7.252, −2.962)	(−0.013, −0.055)
gap	3.4 m	0.10 m

Quoted verbatim (checked at site build): docs/RESULTS.md "The one failure: run 15, and it is a localisation failure" (the M6 fetch matrix in the v1 wedge world; that text entered RESULTS.md on 2026-08-06, per git)
